name: Metabase
description: Open source business intelligence and analytics platform. Create dashboards and explore data without writing SQL.
summary: Metabase is actively releasing patch updates across multiple maintained branches. The latest release is v0.65.3 (Open Source) / v1.65.3 (Enterprise), released on November 6, 2024. Multiple branches (58.x, 63.x, 64.x, 65.x) are receiving concurrent patch releases, indicating active long-term support across versions. Full changelogs for individual patch releases are linked via GitHub compare views at https://github.com/metabase/metabase/releases.

answers.What is the current license?: Open Source edition uses AGPL v3; Enterprise edition has a commercial license. Both are available as separate builds.
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple patch releases across several major branches within days of each other as of November 2024.
answers.Is there a cloud-hosted version availabl: Yes — Metabase offers a managed cloud (Metabase Cloud) referenced in release notes as 'managed cloud'.
answers.Does it support SSO and SAML authenticat: Yes — SSO and SAML are supported as Enterprise/advanced features.
answers.What databases/data sources are supporte: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, SQLite, Oracle, MongoDB, Presto, Druid, SparkSQL, and others via drivers.

alternatives.name: Redash
alternatives.review: Open source, query-focused, simpler feature set.

alternatives.name: Apache Superset
alternatives.review: Apache-licensed, rich visualisation library, steeper setup curve.

alternatives.name: Grafana
alternatives.review: Primarily metrics/time-series but increasingly used for general BI.

alternatives.name: Hex
alternatives.review: Close source, enterprise focus, AI Analytics Platform for your whole team

alternatives.name: Tableau
alternatives.review: Offers far more advanced visualization and analytics capabilities than Metabase but is expensive and not open source.

alternatives.name: Lightdash
alternatives.review: Tightly integrates with dbt for a metrics-layer-first approach, making it more structured than Metabase but requiring a dbt workflow.
